TS0390001.solution: List what the source holds and read one of those names.

TS0390002.message: A read of {limit} rows is not served; ask for between 1 and {max}.
TS0390002.solution: Ask for at most {max} rows, or narrow the read with a filter.

TS0390003.message: Field '{field}' is named with a dot in it, and results cannot be ordered by such a field.
TS0390003.solution: Order by another field. This one can still be filtered on, by escaping the dot that belongs to its name: write it price\\.usd in the shell, and "price\\\\.usd" in JSON, where a lone backslash is not an escape the format allows. Filtering it reads every row, though: an index is written the same way a path is, so a field whose name holds a dot cannot have one.

TS0390004.message: Connector '{connector}' answers reads in its own shape, and this face asks in documents, so its rows cannot be browsed.
TS0390004.solution: Browse a source on one of: {browsable}. This source can still be listed and sized, and it can still be read by a pipeline.

TS0390005.message: Following stopped: the source being followed was deleted.
TS0390005.solution: Declare the source again, or follow a collection of a source that still exists.

TS0390006.message: Following stopped: the stream from the source failed.
TS0390006.solution: Check the server log for what the connector reported, then follow it again.

TS0390007.message: Following stopped after 10 minutes with no changes; the connector instance it held was given back.
TS0390007.solution: Follow it again to keep watching.
